chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qoub bin Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham bin Salem, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali bin Hussain (Allah's blessings be upon them both) used to say: Woe to the one whose singulars overcome his tens. So I said to him: And how is that?

He said: Have you not heard Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, say: «The one who brings a good deed, to him is ten the like of it, and the one who brings a misdeed, he will not be rewarded except by the like of it»

Hence, if one performs one good deed, ten will be written for him, and if one performs one misdeed, one will be written for him. Thus, we seek refuge in Allah from the one who performs, on one day, ten misdeeds and does not (even) have one good deed by which his good deeds can overcome his misdeeds.

key_terms.آحَادُهُ: Singulars (referring to individual bad deeds counted as one)
key_terms.أَعْشَارًا: Tens (referring to good deeds multiplied tenfold)
key_terms.عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا: Ten the like of it (the reward multiplier for good deeds)
key_terms.فَتَغْلِبَ: So that they overcome (referring to good deeds outweighing bad ones)
key_terms.مِثْلُهَا: The like of it (the reward for a single bad deed)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when good deeds are multiplied ten times but bad deeds are not?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine arithmetic of reward and punishment, emphasizing that a single good deed is multiplied ten times while a single sin is recorded as one, creating a precarious balance for the sinner. It serves as a profound ethical warning to seek refuge in God from a state where daily transgressions outpace spiritual merits, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the precision of divine accounting. The hadith underscores the urgency of consistent righteous action to ensure that good deeds ultimately outweigh the accumulation of sins.
